The story strikes an appropriate and effective balance between scene and summary/exposition. It opens with brief exposition to establish the setting and the protagonist's background (his age, his routine, and his wife leaving him), before quickly transitioning into a real-time scene triggered by the sound of the car crash. 

Throughout the rest of the narrative, the story remains grounded in the immediate, unfolding scene—Daniel scrambling down the slope, checking the victim's pulse, calling 911, drapes his jacket over her, and sitting with her as evening falls. Rather than interrupting this scene with dry blocks of exposition, the author cleverly weaves the backstory and summary (the history of Daniel's marriage, his career as a surveyor, his dog's death) into the real-time dialogue of Daniel's monologue to the deceased woman. When narrative summary is used, it smoothly bridges moments of silence and compresses the forty-minute wait for the ambulance, maintaining a meditative pace without losing the emotional immediacy of the scene.
